identificationModule.briefTitle: Ravulizumab in Pregnancies Complicated by Severe Hypertensive Disorders
identificationModule.officialTitle: Clinical Trial on the Use of Ravulizumab in Pregnancies Complicated by Severe Hypertensive Disorders

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The researchers are testing a medication named ravulizumab for the treatment of severe preeclampsia and Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets (HELLP) syndrome.

armGroups.label: Revulizumab Treatment
armGroups.description: Subjects will receive an single-dose infusion of Ravulizumab.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Alternative Complement Pathway Biomarkers at time of delivery
primaryOutcomes.description: Concentration in serum of biomarkers: sMAC, Bb, and C5 at time of delivery

secondaryOutcomes.description: Length of pregnancy measured in number of weeks.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Clinical biomarkers of severe features of preeclampsia and HELLP syndrome
secondaryOutcomes.description: Concentration of clinical biomarkers in serum: creatinine, AST, ALT, LDH and platelets

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Hospitalization length in the postpartum period
secondaryOutcomes.description: Length of hospital stay measured in number of days in hospital stay (peripartum period)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Meningococcal infection after use of ravulizumab
secondaryOutcomes.description: Number of participants to present a meningococcal infection after use of Ravulizumab
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 72 hours up to 3 weeks after Ravulizumab infusion

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Individuals with \< 34 0/7 weeks of gestation.
* Individuals with severe preeclampsia or HELLP features.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Pregnant female patients presenting with disseminated intravascular coagulopathy (DIC).
* Individuals with non-reassuring fetal status requiring delivery, non-viable fetuses, previable pregnancy (\<23 0/7 weeks gestation), stroke, in utero fetal demise, known atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome, familial or acquired thrombocytopenia purpura, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, allergy to Ravulizumab, inability or unwillingness to sign informed consent.
